Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills and is on injured reserve, shifting the line for this game from Ravens -3 (the lookahead) to Jaguars -9.5. That move also comes after backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) was ruled out for this game and third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury. So, the Ravens are in a brutal spot as they look to get back over .500 (Baltimore is 4-4 this season) against the top team in the AFC South. Jacksonville is in a great spot to win the AFC South for the second season in a row, as no other team in the division has more than two wins in 2026. The Jags blew out the Indianapolis Colts – 42-7 – in Week 8, and they’re one of the best defenses in the league, ranking third in EPA/Play and eighth in success rate. Liam Coen’s team is a deserved favorite in this matchup, which could be a tough one to bet on with all the Baltimore injuries. Still, the SI Betting team has curated some picks for Week 9’s Thursday Night showdown, including player props for Lawrence and Derrick Henry. Here’s a breakdown of some of our favorite bets for the action to kick off the final week of the first half of the 2026 season. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are likely out for the game, and their third-string quarterback, Joe Fagnano, is also questionable due to an injury. If he can't go, the Ravens are going to be starting a quarterback who's not on their roster as of me writing this article on Monday night. That leaves the Ravens' only plan of attack being running the football. Unfortunately, they now have to face a Jaguars defense that ranks second in opponent rush EPA and seventh in opponent rush success rate, while giving up fewer yards per carry than any other defense in the league (3.4). I could maybe be convinced to take the points with the Ravens if they had an elite defense, but they're completely average on that side of the ball. Jaguars second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten has played a major role on offense this season, appearing in 55.3 percent of the team’s snaps while registering at least 12 carries in every game. Tuten also has six straight games with two or more receptions, finding the end zone three times through the air and four times overall in his last two games. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. A former No. 1 overall pick, Lawrence is in the MVP conversation this season, but he hasn’t been asked to throw the ball a ton with this Jaguars offense humming on the ground in 2026. Lawrence is averaging under 29 pass attempts per game in 2026, and he threw the ball just 14 times in a 42-7 win over Indianapolis in Week 8. Overall, the star quarterback has just two games (Weeks 5 and 6) where he even attempted 30 passes. So, with the Jaguars heavily favored on a short week, I expect a lighter workload for Lawrence against a Ravens team that has lost three straight and is staring down a lost season with Jackson sidelined. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. This season, Derrick Henry has just four games with over 70 rushing yards, and he’s coming off three straight down performances with 58, 45 and 53 rushing yards, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry during that stretch. The Jaguars are going to stack the box against Henry with all of Baltimore’s quarterback issues, and Jacksonville held Jonathan Taylor to under 30 rushing yards in a blowout in Week 8. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Jacksonville ranks No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Rush, allowing the fewest yards per carry (3.4) and total rushing yards (542) in the league this season. There will not be any Trevor Lawrence-Lamar Jackson round three due to an injury to Jackson. We won't see Tyler Huntley either, with Ravens undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano set to make the start. But there will still be a big stage for the Jaguars, along with a big opportunity. The Jaguars are fighting through their own injuries , losing Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray to season-ending injuries during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Add in running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker being questionable, and the Jaguars are a bit dinged up themselves. But if the Jaguars can overcome the challenge of a road trip against a talented team on a short week, they can do more than prove their mettle. They can be 6-2 entering a stretch where they play the Tennessee Titans twice in a three-week span, giving them a chance to have real-deal playoff-clinching scenarios in December. How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis It is hard not to pick the Jaguars here, and they once again get a clean sweep. It feels weird on the Jaguars end of things, but that is because every game has stakes when you are a good team, and the Jaguars are indeed a good team. The Jaguars have a big chance to make some clear headway toward a potential No. 1 seed in the AFC. They are clumped together right now with the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and Buffalo Bills, but they have to get by a rookie quarterback tonight before facing Cam Ward twice and J.J. McCarthy. If the Jaguars go on a run, they could be 9-2 by right after Thanksgiving. That would make them far more than just contenders in the AFC, and it would start with beating Baltimore. Things could have gotten much more interesting had Jackson been available, but the Jaguars will instead face the dreaded backup quarterback in primetime. Weirdly enough, two of the six losses in the Liam Coen era have been to backup quarterbacks after the Jaguars lost to Jake Browning and Davis Mills a year ago. The only other quarterbacks to beat the Jaguars in the regular-season in that span: Sam Darnold, Matt Stafford, Bo Nix, and CJ Stroud. The Jaguars have beaten other backup and rookie quarterbacks in that span, defeating Jacoby Brissett, Cam Ward (twice), Brady Cook, Riley Leonard, and for some reason, Philip Rivers last season. This season, they have gotten wins against a few guys who have played in the Super Bowl in Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow, and Drake Maye. Add in wins against Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy and Stroud last year, and the argument thatg the Jaguars have beaten up on bad quarterbacks doesn't make much sense. The Jaguars are a good team, and I expect Anthony Campanile's defense to get after the Ravens' young passer. Campanile likes to blitz and pressure quarterbacks into intentionally throwing the ball quickly, which helps the defense dictate where the ball will go in coverage. When you know where the ball is going, you can make plays on it or tackle and rally and make stops like the Jaguars have done for two years. According to NextGenStats, Jacksonville has generated a 39.6% pressure rate this season (8th-highest), and its pressures have arrived in 2.43 seconds on average, the quickest in the NFL. Seven of Jacksonville's pressures have resulted in turnovers, tied for the most in the league, and the Jaguars have generated 31 unblocked pressures, tied for second-most. This means the Jaguars' pressures are leading to big plays on the back end, and they force the issue with opposing quarterbacks. Against a young quarterback and a running game that has lesser numbers without Lamar Jackson, I think the Jaguars win this game with field position and red-zone stops. Jaguars 30, Ravens 13. away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.headline: Lamar Jackson's message to Ravens revealed in NFL rumors amid injury, return buzz and losing streak
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is aiming to return during the 2026 NFL season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . After playing the first three games of the year, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain, returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Buffalo Bills. His return was brief, however, as he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive drive. Rapoport reported that Jackson spoke to the team and delivered an "energizing" and "exciting" message. The overall theme was to "just stay alive" until he's healthy enough to be back on the field. The Ravens are last in the AFC North at 4-5 following Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The combined absences of Jackson and Tyler Huntley were glaring as third-stringer Joe Fagnano threw for 60 yards and two interceptions on 18 attempts. Jackson has unfortunately had another injury-riddled year. The injury required surgery, and the two-time MVP was placed on the injured reserve immediately after the game. Huntley came in for Jackson after his injury, but he was forced to exit soon after because of a turf toe injury. A day after the Jaguars loss, Baltimore acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett is a significant upgrade from Fagnano and may be enough for the team to keep its head above water in the weeks ahead. It's clear Jackson isn't throwing away the rest of the season, and that attitude is bound to spread to the rest of the locker room.

Jackson dealt with a high-ankle sprain before a much-needed return last week against the Buffalo Bills . However, on his first snap of the game, his throwing hand collided with Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau’s hand. He was placed on the injured reserved after needing surgery to repair his thumb. So, Tyler "Snoop" Huntley had to resume his role as the team’s starter, doing so in the games Jackson missed earlier in the season. But Huntley suffered a turf toe injury in the same Bills matchup, knocking him out for the remainder of the season. That led to emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano, a rookie out of UConn, taking over in a 36-10 loss to the Bills. The Ravens made the move to trade for Brissett after the Arizona Cardinals benched him in the second half of a comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8, where head coach Mike LaFleur gave the reins to Gardner Minshew, and later named rookie Carson Beck his backup entering Week 9. The Baltimore Ravens ’ playoff hopes are teetering amid quarterback injury issues and a four-game losing streak, which includes a 33-10 rout by the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. While Baltimore did trade for Jacoby Brissett to hopefully put an end to their signal-caller woes, rumors have begun swirling around one of the team’s stars: running back Derrick Henry . The NFL trade deadline is on Tuesday, and some were of the belief the Ravens would at least listen to trade offers for the 32-year-old veteran back – a team that could be one piece like Henry away from a complete squad ready for a Super Bowl run. The speculation surrounded two of Henry’s former head coaches, with John Harbaugh and the New York Giants reportedly in the aggressive buying stage, and running back is where they seem to be looking. The Giants are among those very interested in Jonathan Taylor with the Indianapolis Colts. New England Patriots’ Mike Vrabel could’ve also been a good spot for a Henry reunion, especially given that TreVeyon Henderson was just hospitalized after suffering "unexplainable" neurological symptoms. Henry is a key cog in making this Declan Doyle-led offense work for the Ravens, but it hasn’t looked that way among recent quarterback injuries, most notably to two-time MVP Lamar Jackson. Bagent immediately stood out as a potential trade option for Baltimore because Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle came from the Chicago Bears where the two worked together last season. Few teams are harder to figure out right now than the Colts, even though they have acknowledged their need to sell by trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jones' availability might be even harder to figure out because head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Monday he will remain the starting quarterback. Of the potential quarterback options mentioned by Fowler and Graziano, Brissett might be the most available. He was benched by the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in favor of Gardner Minshew II, who led the offense to 23 points in the fourth quarter and overtime in a 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. There's no good situation for the Ravens right now because Tyler Huntley also suffered a turf toe injury that is expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set to make his first career start on Thursday night against the Jaguars. It has not been determined if Jackson will miss the rest of the season, but an IR stint will keep him out for at least the next four weeks. The schedule does help them because they have a bye in Week 13, meaning Jackson could theoretically be back on Dec. 13 with five games remaining. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the 36-10 loss to Buffalo that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. home.headline: Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens had a rough afternoon, starting with the first offensive play of the game when quarterback Lamar Jackson hit Bills defender Greg Rousseau's arm, causing Jackson to suffer a thumb injury and not return. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley , also didn't last long. Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half and didn't return. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that Huntley suffered a turf toe injury. Huntley and Jackson could both miss time, and Jackson is confirmed out for at least four weeks. Head coach Jesse Minter said postgame that Jackson will be placed on injured reserve and will undergo surgery on his right thumb. Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report Unlock the latest Heavy on Ravens news — direct to your inbox. This was Jackson first game back after he suffered an ankle injury against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 and missed the last three games. "Ravens QB Tyler "Snoop" Huntley suffered what is thought to be a turf toe injury today at Buffalo, per source," Schefter wrote on X. "He is expected to undergo an MRI tomorrow to determine how much time if any he could miss." Ravens Could Be Down Jackson and Huntley for a While The Ravens turned to quarterback Joe Fagnano after losing Huntley, and he had a tough afternoon, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and one interception. Minter also said, "We'll see" on whether Jackson will miss the rest of the season. Huntley has started three games this season, and the Ravens are 1-2. The Ravens beat the Falcons in his first start of the season but lost the last two against the Browns and Bengals. Losing your starting quarterback and backup in the same game is never good. It's even worse when this happens during a short week. The Ravens will have a quick turnaround as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. The Jaguars are coming off a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday to move to 5-2. Baltimore might not have a chance to play Huntley even if he can go, since it's hard to come back from an injury on a shorter week with less than four full days to recover. It will also be difficult for the Ravens to bring in a quarterback to play on Thursday, even if they lack confidence in Fagnano. The Ravens might have to get by with Fagnano starting on Thursday, then reevaluate options when they have about 10 days off between their games against the Jaguars and the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16. home.headline: Desperate Baltimore Ravens seal huge NFL quarterback trade after Jackson and Huntley injuries
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens have found a fix to their quarterback injury woes by trading for Arizona Cardinals star Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens are down to third-choice undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , leaving general manager Eric DaCosta desperately scrabbling around for a long-term solution. NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report on Wednesday that the Ravens are now finalizing a trade for Brissett, with the deal set to be completed over the weekend. Fagnano will therefore be on the field for Baltimore on Thursday night, before Brissett takes the quarterback reins in Week 10 for the Monday Night Football showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett had become a prime trade candidate in Arizona after being benched midgame against the Dallas Cowboys and then dropped to QB3 on the depth chart. He started the first eight games of the season for Arizona this season, going 3-5 with a 63.3% pass completion. After Brissett was benched during the loss to the Cowboys, the starting job was handed to Gardner Minshew, with Carson Beck the backup. West Palm Beach native Brissett will join his seventh NFL team in Baltimore, in his 11th season in the league. He was first selected by the New England Patriots in the third round of the 2016 Draft, going on to win the Super Bowl as Tom Brady's backup in his first season. He was traded to the Colts after his rookie season and was the starter there in 2017 and 2019, before alternating as a back-up and starter in Miami, Cleveland, Washington and back in New England, before eventually landing in Arizona. In March 2025 he signed a two-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals and played in 14 games last season. Despite reworking his contract to increase his compensation for the 2026 season, he will become a free agent at the end of the campaign, unless he agrees new terms in Baltimore.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features many of the league's top offensive stars Getty Images Following a week without an international game, the NFL heads back overseas in Week 9 when it sends the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals to Spain. The Bernabéu will play host to American football for the second time in as many years as two divisional contenders descend upon Madrid. The Bengals are in search of their first win away from American soil in franchise history after going 0-1-1 in their previous two opportunities (the most recent contest dating back to 2019), while the Falcons seek to improve to .500 in games abroad. Atlanta is 2-3 away from the United States and last season lost in Berlin. This contest pits one of the league's hottest teams against a squad that aims to reestablish positive momentum. Cincinnati rides a three-game win streak into the Madrid Game and scored no fewer than 31 points in any of those triumphs, albeit with two of the matchups coming against bottom-tier competition. Atlanta, on the other hand, lost in two of its last three outings and went scoreless in its most recent showing. Both sides are alive and well in their respective divisions, but the context between the two differs greatly. The Falcons are just a half game back of first place in the NFC South, which may be the weakest division in football with no teams at or above .500 through the season's first two months. The Bengals' position at half a game out of the AFC North lead is the superior standing considering three teams own winning records. Where to watch Falcons vs. Bengals live Date: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location: Bernabéu (Madrid) TV: NFL Network, stream on fubo Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Falcons vs. Bengals key storylines Bijan Robinson and Drake London see bounce-back opportunity: It is no small feat to keep one of the NFL's top running back-wide receiver tandems in check, but how much credit do the Tampa Bay Buccaneers deserve for doing so in Week 8? With due respect to a formidable defense, the weather in that shutout might have had more to do with the Falcons going scoreless than anything else. A major one-week swing could be in store for this duo as it squares off against a Cincinnati unit that just allowed the Tennessee Titans to rack up 36 points. Robinson remains the league's rushing leader with 780 yards on the year, and London stands sixth in receiving yards at 624. If the Bengals could not keep the Titans in check, they will have their hands even more full with these two stars. Tee Higgins reaches new echelon: Higgins has long played second fiddle to Ja'Marr Chase in the otherworldly Bengals passing attack but is now on level ground with his superstar teammate. Both saw exactly 61 targets across their first seven games, and both grabbed 43 catches on those opportunities. But Higgins has been the far more efficient receiver of the two with 726 yards. That ranks second in the NFL, only to potential repeat Offensive Player of the Year winner Jaxon Smith-Njigba . This is the best version of Higgins the league has seen, and it is on pace for historic production . James Pearce Jr . to make season debut: The NFL reinstated Pearce after he served an eight-game suspension for a violation of the league's personal conduct policy, which makes him eligible to play for the first time this season in Week 9. Atlanta has been surprisingly disruptive on the defensive front without the second-year pass rusher, who faced felony charges this offseason following a domestic dispute but is on track to have those charges dropped. A unit that ranks sixth in quarterback pressure rate may climb even closer to the top of the leaderboard and perhaps improve its sack totals upon Pearce's insertion into the lineup, because he logged 10.5 sacks as a rookie despite starting only three games. Joe Burrow on MVP pace: Only two quarterbacks ( Josh Allen and Brock Purdy ) have shorter odds, via DraftKings Sportsbook, to win the NFL's top individual award. Burrow leads both of them in touchdowns with a league-best 20, and he is a mere 0.1 points away from the NFL lead in passer rating at 111.6. This is so far the most efficient season of Burrow's stellar career, which is a pleasant development of an offense that missed him dearly when he missed a combined 16 games over the last three seasons due to injuries. The Falcons kept Purdy in check when they upset him and the San Francisco 49ers two weeks ago, but Burrow presents an even greater challenge and has a healthier supporting cast than the one Purdy brought into the Week 7 contest. Falcons vs. Bengals prediction Fans of American football in Spain are in for a treat, because this game has all the makings of a shootout. There is not an offense in the NFL that is clicking quite like the Bengals over the last three weeks, and between Burrow, Chase, Higgins, London and Robinson, five of the biggest names in football will be in action in a star-studded battle. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . should bounce back from last week's dreadful 8-for-24 showing in the rain, so Atlanta ought to have enough juice to keep pace with a team that is averaging 36.3 points per game since Oct. 11. In a matchup where points will be aplenty, the team with the better defense holds the edge. It is not as though Atlanta is vastly superior on that side of the ball, but it is much more reliable and is about to insert one of its projected top producers into the lineup for the first time this season. There is not a more opportune time for a disruptive pass rusher like Pearce to make his first appearance than against arguably the best quarterback in the NFL. That alone could be the difference in a high-variance matchup like this one. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. Pick: Bills 21, Vikings 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

Joe Burrow and the Bengals survived a scare against the Tennessee Titans in Week 8, winning in overtime despite three interceptions from their star quarterback. Cincinnati is now 5-2 through eight weeks and is in the driver's seat to win the AFC North, sitting as an odds-on favorite at the best betting sites . Even though the Bengals are technically the road team in this matchup, oddsmakers have set them as favorites against a Falcons team that has been super up and down in 2026. Atlanta started the season with back-to-back losses without Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback, but it's 3-3 since his return, turning in a huge victory over the San Francisco 49ers in Week 7. However, Penix threw four picks in a rain-filled game against Tampa Bay in Week 8, dropping the Falcons to 3-5 this season. They need as many wins as they can get if they want to stay in the mix to win the NFC South in 2026. There are a ton of ways to bet on this international game and it kicks off a huge 13-game slate on Sunday (15 games in total in Week 9). All week long our team at SI Betting has made game picks, player prop selections and more to help our readers decide on their wagers for this Bengals vs. Falcons showdown. I compiled some of our favorites all into one spot to help you prepare for this matchup in Madrid. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Bengals vs. Falcons Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Cincinnati Bengals -3 (-112) vs. Atlanta Falcons – Iain MacMillan Bijan Robinson OVER 92.5 Rushing Yards (-111) – Peter Dewey Tee Higgins OVER 78.5 Receiving Yards (-111) – Peter Dewey Ja’Marr Chase Anytime TD (-115) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan picks every single game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s targeting the Bengals as the “road team” in this international matchup on Sunday: The Falcons' handful of impressive performances this season have convinced people this team is better than they are. They continue to have plenty of issues on both sides of the ball. Their defense has regressed after a strong start to the season, and Michael Penix Jr. displays accuracy issues on a weekly basis. He now ranks 32nd out of 35 starting quarterbacks this season in completion percentage over expected. play and 12th in defensive weighted EPA per play. Don't be fooled into thinking their defense is bad because of a down game against the Titans last week. They certainly aren't an elite unit, but an average defense is good enough to let the Cincinnati offense do its thing to win games. The most important aspect of the Bengals' defense is its ability to stop the run. They rank sixth in opponent rush success rate, and we've already seen the Falcons fail to produce offensively when facing strong run defenses like the Steelers' and Buccaneers'. Falcons running back Bijan Robinson has just two 100-yard games in the 2026 season and has failed to clear 92.5 rushing yards in six of his eight matchups. Yet, I’m buying him against a Cincinnati defense that is just 20th in the league in EPA/Rush in the 2026 season. The Bengals were just torched by Tony Pollard and a bad Tennessee offense in Week 8, and they’re allowing 4.8 yards per carry in the 2026 season – the fourth-most in the NFL. That’s a great sign for Robinson, who has at least 19 carries in five of his games and is averaging 5.2 yards per carry overall. If the Falcons can commit to giving him around 20 touches, he should soar past this number against a Cincy defense that has come back to earth after a fast start to 2026. Bengals star wideout Tee Higgins has stayed healthy – so far – in the 2026 season, and it’s done wonders for the Bengals’ offense. Cincinnati is fourth in the league in EPA/Pass, and it may look to attack through the air against a Falcons defense that is third in the league in EPA/Rush but just 14th in EPA/Pass. This comes after Atlanta didn’t allow a single competition in a Week 8 loss in the rain to Tampa Bay. Higgins has been the yardage guy for the Cincy offense this season, catching 43 of his 61 targets for 726 yards and four scores in seven games. He’s averaging over 100 yards per game and has cleared 90 yards in five games this season (and 100 in three). He’s coming off an 11-target game in Week 8 and has 303 receiving yards in two games since the team’s Week 6 bye. He’s a must bet against Atlanta on Sunday. Speaking of star wideouts, I’m eyeing Ja’Marr Chase to find the end zone for the seventh time in eight games on Sunday. Chase has been a touchdown machine for the Bengals, only failing to score in Week 1 and Week 4 (he left Week 4 with a concussion). The Falcons have allowed just 11 passing scores this season, but Joe Burrow has been on an absolute heater in recent weeks, throwing 13 touchdown passes over his last three games. He’s making things look easy for a Cincy offense that is now fourth in EPA/Pass. Chase is almost always going to be minus money to find the end zone, but I don’t mind this price since he’s always going to have a huge target share (61 in seven games) for this Bengals offense. The Bengals have been a high-scoring team in the Burrow era, but lately, they’ve taken things a step further. The star quarterback has thrown four or more touchdowns in each of his last three games, finding Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Mike Gesicki with ease as the Bengals have rolled to a 5-2 start. While the Falcons are a top-10 team in the league in EPA/Play on defense this season, they struggled against the run in a loss to Tampa Bay last week and are now just 3-5 in the 2026 season. Penix was especially rough in Week 8, getting picked off four times in a rain-soaked game on the road. The Falcons still have plenty of weapons on offense, including first-round picks Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. That puts them in a spot to compete with this Bengals team if Penix is able to flip the script in Week 9. One of the most exciting ways to bet on a standalone game in the NFL is the anytime touchdown scorer market. All you need to do is pick a player to score a touchdown, and if they do, your bet will cash. With a ton of great playmakers in action and a ton of points expected on Sunday in Madrid, I narrowed things down to three players to find the end zone in Week 9. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Bengals vs. Falcons Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Ja’Marr Chase Anytime TD (-115) Chase has been a touchdown machine for the Bengals, only failing to score in Week 1 and Week 4 (he left Week 4 with a concussion). The Falcons have allowed just 11 passing scores this season, but Joe Burrow has been on an absolute heater in recent weeks, throwing 13 touchdown passes over his last three games. He’s making things look easy for a Cincy offense that is now fourth in EPA/Pass. Chase is almost always going to be minus money to find the end zone, but I don’t mind this price since he’s always going to have a huge target share (61 in seven games) for this Bengals offense. Mike Gesicki Anytime TD (+220) It’s pretty shocking that Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki is +220 to find the end zone on Sunday, as he’s scored in six of his seven games despite the fact that he’s played just 48.3 percent of the offensive snaps. In fact, Gesicki has a touchdown in every game that he’s received a target from Joe Burrow (he was not targeted in Week 2). Overall, Gesicki has just 24 targets and 17 catches in seven games, but he’s clearly a threat in the red zone for one of the highest-scoring offenses in the league. Atlanta has allowed four scores to opposing tight ends in 2026, and it has been worse against the pass (14th in EPA/Pass) than the run (third in EPA/Rush). I expect Burrow and the Bengals to attack through the air in Madrid. The Colts also traded All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson last week, leaving a less experienced offensive line in front of Jones. That gives Quinnen Williams and the Dallas pass rush a real opportunity after producing five sacks against Arizona. If Dallas can force Indianapolis into obvious passing situations, this is the type of matchup where the defense should finally create pressure without constantly needing to blitz. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should look at the Indianapolis defense and see an opportunity to rediscover its running game. The Colts are allowing 4.9 yards per carry, and their defensive front no longer includes DeForest Buckner after he was traded to San Francisco. Dallas ran the ball 39 times against Arizona but gained only 93 yards, so simply calling more runs is not enough. Brian Schottenheimer needs to find the concepts and directions that actually create space for Javonte Williams rather than repeatedly running into crowded areas. Establishing Williams would make life considerably easier for Dak Prescott. Dallas is still scoring 27 points per game, seventh in the NFL, while Prescott has 14 touchdowns against five interceptions. Indianapolis has only two interceptions all season and has just traded away its best interior pass rusher, so there should be opportunities if Dallas stays ahead of the chains. CeeDee Lamb remains the obvious focal point, although Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward give Indianapolis two experienced cornerbacks capable of making the outside matchups difficult. That makes Jake Ferguson's ankle injury particularly important but he is questionable, while George Pickens was limited by a hamstring issue. The Cowboys cannot repeat what happened late against Arizona, when the offense had chances to put the game away but failed to finish drives. Indianapolis has conceded 23 touchdowns while scoring only 15 itself, and Jacksonville just put 42 points on this defense. Dallas should attack with balance, use play-action once Williams gets going and force a Colts defense without Buckner to defend the entire field. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (4-4) Maybe it's just all getting to me, but I'm starting to worry this team is fundamentally and irreparably broken. It feels good like the collapse will continue. Colts 30 Cowboys 27 Brandon Loree (5-3) The Cowboys play the Indianapolis Colts every four years, so the last win at Lucas Oil Stadium feels like a lifetime ago. If you go back and watch that game, I think this Sunday could have a similar formula. The Colts can't get going on offense and have multiple turnovers, but stick around until the very end. The Cowboys need to decide whether they're a pass team or a run team and stick to that identity. Flipping back and forth is what's causing this inconsistency. It's close, but if this Cowboys team can't beat this version of Indy, all hope is lost. I think the Cowboys win 33-24. Dyllan Rivers (4-4) The floundering Cowboys take on the fire sale Colts this week. As of this prediction, Jonathan Taylor is still wearing white and blue. If that holds true, he'll be the target to eliminate on Sunday. After watching Tyler Allgeier make swiss cheese of the run defense, forgive me if I lack confidence in their ability to limit the Colts running back. Still, the pattern suggests Dallas will win this one. So with a big sigh and shrug, give me the Cowboys 31-24. Matt Holleran (4-4) I am very worried that this Cowboys team is broken upon repair. If this is the case, Sunday's matchup against the Colts could end up being the lowest point of an already very low season. I have no confidence this team will show any fight or bounce back, even in a very winnable matchup. I hope I'm wrong, but I see this game being the culmination of the downward spiral as Dallas hits an even lower rock bottom. Give me Indy, 33-20. Mike Poland (3-5) Dallas should bounce back this weekend (well that's what I'm hoping), and this matchup against Indianapolis gives them the perfect opportunity to do it. The Cowboys rank seventh-best in the NFL in points per game, while the Colts have the league's worst defenses, allowing 28 points per game. The Colts have also struggled offensively, with Daniel Jones throwing nine interceptions to just five touchdowns. I'm expecting a positive outlook from Dallas and a much-needed victory to get their season moving in the right direction with the Cowboys winning 31-17. Or maybe I'm just being stupidly optimistic.

home.headline: Latest Dallas Cowboys injury report brings worrying news for a banged-up defense ahead of Week 9 matchup with Colts
home.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys are running out of healthy bodies in the secondary with the Indianapolis Colts coming to town. And a key defender popped up on the injury report out of nowhere. When Porter Jr. was a participant on Wednesday, those concerns eased a bit. On Thursday, however, the Cowboys listed him as a limited participant again. Speaking of the secondary, safeties Caleb Downs and PJ Locke remain in the concussion protocol. Each was upgraded from a non-participant on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday. NFL players who enter the protocol often miss at least one week, but there's no set minimum number of days a player has to sit. In 2023, CBS Sports insider Jonathan Jones reported that the median return from a concussion is nine days. At least Downs and Locke took a significant step forward by getting back to on-field activity as limited participants. Sticking with the defense, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is a new addition to the report. He wasn't listed on Wednesday, but he was limited on Thursday with a hamstring/back injury. Overshown didn't play from Week 1 against the New York Giants until he returned against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7. Seeing him back on the injury report isn't encouraging. It doesn't necessarily mean he'll be out on Sunday. As for the rest of the linebacker group, Dee Winters continues to trend in the right direction. He was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice and is in line to return to the active roster. Wide receiver George Pickens remains on the report after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. He's now listed with only a hamstring injury, not a shoulder injury. At tight end, Luke Schoonmaker was limited again on Thursday. He missed the last game against the Cardinals with a groin injury, and his status for Week 9 might matter more than expected. Jake Ferguson missed his second straight practice of the week after getting hurt early against Arizona. Elsewhere, edge rusher Malachi Lawrence and returner KaVontae Turpin were non-participants. Offensive tackle Tyler Smith was limited on both Wednesday and Thursday with an ankle injury, but the Cowboys didn't appear concerned about his availability for Week 9. The Dolphins, which have won just one game this season (1-6), are coming off a 24-19 defeat at the hands of the New England Patriots. Meanwhile, Detroit prevailed against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings a week ago, 19-15. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 9 matchup with Miami. Christian Booher The Detroit Lions have had to navigate some uncharted territory emotionally after the injury to linebacker Jack Campbell. A leader of the defense, Campbell's absence will be tough to account for as he had a huge impact on the operation. While Derrick Barnes is a veteran with plenty of experience, he could need some time to adjust to the new role he's expected to be in. However, I think Dan Campbell's mettle as a motivator will be tested. He was adamant about the importance of remaining focused amidst the adversity, and I think he'll have the team ready to go. They could start slow, but I expect that the offense will get it together quickly. Even with some injuries on the defensive end, the Lions are able to get enough stops to earn a victory in Sunday's game. Lions 38, Dolphins 27 Yes, the Lions will be playing without multiple core defenders on Sunday in Miami (i.e. Jack Campbell, D.J. Reed and DJ Wonnum). And sure, Detroit could be looking ahead to its highly-anticipated Week 10 clash with the New England Patriots in Germany. However, I don't think any of that will matter in the Lions’ Week 9 contest with the 1-6 Dolphins. Yes, Miami is likely better than that record indicates. Yet, Detroit, even with the various injuries, is still the superior team, and I believe will show that early and often on Sunday. Deploying their “next man up” mantra, the Lions pull out a gritty win on the road against the Dolphins. Lions 31, Dolphins 20 John Maakaron The Detroit Lions are hoping to avoid an emotional letdown for multiple reasons. The team is coming off a tough victory against a division rival in the Minnesota Vikings. Unfortunately, linebacker and defensive captain Jack Campbell will be out of action for the foreseeable future after being carted off the field last week. Some may think the Dolphins are a trap game, but Dan Campbell's squad should rally and find the resolve needed to come away with the victory this week. Campbell's injury may also galvanize the roster beyond Week 9, similar to how the 1991 team rallied after Mike Utley suffered a serious injury. Detroit's offense should be able to move the football up and down the field against a young Dolphins team that is still learning how to close out games and win with a new head coach. Tight end Sam LaPorta could be targeted heavily this week, as the Dolphins' defense has given up plenty of yards to opposing tight ends on a weekly basis. Lions 24, Dolphins 17 Emmett Matasovsky The Lions take on the Miami Dolphins, which were not projected to be that great this year. So far, the Dolphins have met that expectation, ranking among the worst in the league. However, that screams “trap game,” especially with the Munich game next week and the Lions’ minds obviously and rightfully elsewhere with the Jack Campbell injury. The key to the game here is to force more turnovers with quick pressure and to stuff the run game, as the Lions are missing three expected contributors from their linebackers room alone. On paper, this should be an easy Lions victory. Personally, I think the Lions take full control during the game and fly home from Miami with an easy victory after 175 total yards from Jahmyr Gibbs and 100 yards and a touchdown from Amon-Ra St. Brown. Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami. As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit . Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory . picks.headline: Roundtable: Previewing Lions Week 9 Matchup Against Dolphins
picks.blurb: Roundtable: Previewing Lions Week 9 Matchup Against Dolphins Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 9 matchup with the Miami Dolphins. 1. Do you see any chance of a letdown against Dolphins? Christian Booher: I think with the emotions that have been felt throughout the week, there is a chance that the Lions come out sluggish against Miami. The Jack Campbell injury has been tough for many to process given how severe it was, and the Lions will be without a key player within their defense. His absence will have a big impact, and as a result the defense in particular could struggle. Still, Dan Campbell has proven to be one of the league's best motivators. Because of that, I think the Lions will come out with plenty of fire against the Dolphins. Vito Chirco: Even with all the injuries, I just don't see it. I think Miami is a bit better than its 1-6 record indicates, based on how close it's been in a variety of its losses this season. However, that doesn't mean the Jeff Hafley-led team is going to surprise Dan Campbell's squad on Sunday. I still believe Detroit plays more than well enough to emerge victorious in the Week 9 contest. Emmett Matasovsky: I think there is very much a chance, but I am not saying it is a high one, mind you. The Lions have had an emotional week with Jack Campbell’s injury, and this Dolphins team is one that gets overlooked in the stretch. Additionally, Malik Willis being a mobile quarterback always makes this a potential trap game for Detroit, given its struggles in the Campbell era with mobile quarterbacks. 2. Can Jack Campbell’s injury actually serve as a rallying cry this year for the Lions? Booher : I do think the team will rally around Campbell, and we've already started to see elements of that this year. Campbell was a captain of the defense and a massive leader in the locker room. He leaves big shoes to fill for the time being, but I think the Lions will embrace the challenge and they do have the depth to navigate this injury. Chirco : Yes, I believe it could have that effect. It doesn't take away from the fact that the Lions still need to make a move or two to upgrade their defense. But yes, I believe that Dan Campbell and the players will use Jack Campbell's injury as an extra source of motivation the rest of the way this season. Matasovsky : I absolutely think it can. Campbell is a leader for this locker room and one of the most productive members on defense. The linebacker’s presence will be sorely missed, but the unity in the team at this time can also lead to a more close-knit locker room and better performance. That said, it is not going to be easy to replace the veteran backer, especially with the injuries to Devin White and Jimmy Rolder both factored in. There are not many players with experience in Kelvin Sheppard’s system left. 3. Who do you think the Lions must land at trade deadline? Booher : The Lions need to get a cornerback. D.J. Reed is out Sunday, so the team will get a long look at its depth throughout the game. If things don't go well, it will further amplify the need for general manager Brad Holmes and company. Of the options expected to be available, I think Riq Woolen is the best fit for the defense. He has high-level experience having won a Super Bowl last year, and can be extremely good in Detroit's scheme. Donte Jackson of the Los Angeles Chargers is another good veteran option, though he has had some injury issues this year. Chirco : I'd like to see the Lions make a move for Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker. But because of the draft capital that would likely be involved to land Baker, I don't envision it being very likely. That's why I'm going to say Detroit GM Brad Holmes must go out and land Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen. Woolen would be a solid acquisition for Detroit's secondary and provide the organization with a capable No. 2 corner behind D.J. Reed. If I'm Holmes, I'm targeting Woolen leading into Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Matasovsky : A true impact corner, and for me, the ideal target is Riq Woolen from the Philadelphia Eagles. Another much more expensive option would be Sauce Gardner from the Indianapolis Colts, although I am not sure if I see the returns outweighing multiple first round picks. A shutdown corner alongside a healthy Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch makes things scary for opposing offenses, and that is before a healthy DJ Wonnum, Alim McNeill, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Aidan Hutchinson are chasing quarterbacks down. 4. Who will be Lions game MVP against Dolphins? Booher : I think the defense will come up big in Sunday's game. With Campbell out, they'll be motivated to produce to show support for their injured teammate. Because of that, I think Aidan Hutchinson will lead the charge and get after Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis. I think Hutchinson sets the tone with an early sack and generates a turnover with a strip-sack later in the game to help fuel the team to a win. Chirco : I'm going to go with Jameson Williams, who has scored each of his five touchdowns over the course of the last three weeks. With Amon-Ra St. Brown a bit banged up, I believe that Williams will put together another strong effort and record his fourth straight game with a TD reception. Matasovsky : I think Jahmyr Gibbs will be the game MVP. Sonic is going to get his yards, and this is not a defense that could compete with any NFC North offense on a good day, let alone a mostly healthy Lions offense. Gibbs is going to top 100 yards by the midway point of the third quarter and finish at 175 total yards on the day, if I predict. 5. Which NFC team concerns you the most right now? Booher : There are a pair of teams that I think match up well with the Lions and could give them some fits. One is the San Francisco 49ers. When they're clicking, the 49ers are a tough team to beat due to their array of weapons such as running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle. I also think the Bears could give the Lions some fits. Ben Johnson is one of the best offensive minds in football, and Caleb Williams has been playing at a very high level. That Thanksgiving matchup is looming, and could have massive divisional stakes. Chirco : It's the Bears with Caleb Williams, Jeffery Simmons and the great collection of talent they've assembled. They are the one team that might be better than the Lions in the NFC North, which adds further intrigue to their Thanksgiving Day clash with Ben Johnson's team. Matasovsky : It’s the NFL, so any given Sunday. Mostly kidding. On a real note, the San Francisco 49ers look dominant and just re-acquired DeForest Buckner, which makes them a massive threat. If Brandon Aiyuk pays his fines and is in condition to play, they gain another weapon on offense, too. It is going to be hard to get through that San Francisco team, and they are my midway pick for the NFC representative in the Super Bowl thus far. away.headline: Detroit Lions Player Says He Doesn't Yet Have Full Movement In His Body After Terrifying Injury
away.blurb: “Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital,” the team shared. “Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.” By Carly Ledbetter Senior Reporter, HuffPost LOADING ERROR LOADING Detroit Lions player Jack Campbell has issued his first statement on his condition, just days after enduring a terrifying neck injury in a game against the Vikings. Campbell, 26, did not appear to be moving while he was taken off the field, as his teammates looked on with tears and concern. Campbell said Wednesday he is still working on regaining movement in his body, though he does have full movement in his lower body at this time. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” he said in a statement. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger.” Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions lays on the ground after being injured on a play during the fourth quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1. Mike Mulholland via Getty Images “I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” he added. “I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.” Dan Campbell, head coach for the Detroit Lions, previously spoke about visiting Campbell in the hospital, though he declined to share the specifics of his injury or his progress. “I got to go see him last night, it was good, it was positive,” Campbell said during a press conference on Monday. “Got to see his parents, talk to his wife, and everybody’s in good spirits. It’s about the recovery, and it’s a small setback.” Both Lions and Vikings players took a knee on the turf as Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell (not pictured) received medical treatment. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Advertisement The Lions also kept details about Campbell’s injury vague in a statement shared on Monday. Campbell and his wife, Megan, recently welcomed a 4-month-old son named Cooper. Read Campbell’s full statement below: STATEMENT FROM JACK CAMPBELL My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such…

Dave Birkett Rainer Sabin Christian Romo Carlos Monarrez Jeff Seidel Shawn Windsor Detroit Free Press Nov. 8, 2026, 5:04 a.m. ET Hear this story View Comments The Detroit Lions enter their Week 9 matchup with heavy hearts and a sense of purpose. A week after the scary injury to linebacker Jack Campbell that landed him in the hospital, the Lions will take the field trying to make No. 46 proud. And they have a pretty good chance to do so against what is, on paper, an overmatched Miami Dolphins team. The Dolphins (1-6) came into the season as a popular pick to finish last in the NFL and have lived up to those expectations so far. Can the Lions (5-2) take care of business and continue their climb up the NFC standings? Our Free Press experts make their picks: It's been an emotional week for the Lions, and while there will be a crash to pay for it at some point, I don't think that happens now. The Lions are a much more talented team than the Dolphins, even with their injury problems, and the history of teams playing for a teammate who suffers a catastrophic injury on the field are clear. The 2022 Buffalo Bills won their next two games after Damar Hamlin went into cardiac arrest on the field; the 2017 Pittsburgh Steelers won three of four after Ryan Shazier's scary spinal-cord injury; and the 1991 Lions won six straight after Mike Utley was paralyzed. The Dolphins are a scrappy team that's played a bunch of close games of late, but they don't have the guns to compete with the Lions. The pick: Lions 35, Dolphins 17 The Dolphins may be better than their 1-6 record indicates and may show some pluck against an ailing Lions defense, but Detroit knows how much it needs to stack wins against lesser opponents, especially in a division as tough as the NFC North. They'll be prepared, especially if they answer the call to play on behalf of their injured teammate. The pick: Lions 31, Dolphins 24. After all, they have won three straight games and just knocked off the last undefeated team, Minnesota. The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson . Here are our staff predictions. Grant Chachere , Lead Writer: W 24-10 This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints. Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin . Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase. This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up. However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis . Saints 24 Browns 10 Doug Joubert , Publisher: L 28-17 The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing. This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend. The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game. These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no. The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going. This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept). I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win. I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too. And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it.
