Tyson, the eighth overall pick in this year’s draft, has been out since getting hurt Aug. 13 with a hamstring injury and missed the Saints’ first seven games, but he returned to practice this week. Tyson’s return should help a Saints offense that has been uneven this season. The Saints rank 14th in points per game, but 23rd in total offense. Most of the team’s struggles have centered around the run game — the Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti on Monday — but Tyson provides another dynamic weapon in the passing game, which could help open up New Orleans’ rushing attack. The Saints had previously listed Tyson as questionable. The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night. It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history. What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions. Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss. However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season. Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career. Vikings sack Bills QB Josh Allen more than five times Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics: Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed) Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (56.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8) Sack rate (11%) QB pressure rate (46%) Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century) They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks. Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career. Cowboys hold the Colts to under 20 points The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL. However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season. Jets' Braelon Allen goes off against Chiefs New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548. Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008. Dolphins hold Lions QB Jared Goff to under 200 passing yards The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success. Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25). However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game. Nabers should be able to continue his great stretch in Philadelphia, and I’d consider laddering him up to 100+ yards at +242, or even 110+ yards for the fifth straight week at +343. Saquon Barkley is currently dealing with some injuries, but I’d be shocked if he doesn’t play this week against his former team. He’s suited up in each of the last two weeks, scoring against the Cowboys and Commanders. Barkley scored two touchdowns in the home game against the Giants last season, and I think he’ll find the end zone again this week. He is one of the Eagles’ few healthy offensive weapons, after all. away.blurb: Cam Skattebo’s availability remains a concern for the New York Giants entering Sunday’s NFC East matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles . New York’s leading rusher is listed as doubtful with a hamstring injury, leaving the Giants preparing to play without a key piece of their offense. Skattebo did not participate in practice Wednesday or Thursday before being listed as limited Friday on the official injury report. That return provided some progress, but his doubtful designation means he is unlikely to play. New York enters the matchup at 4-2-1, while Philadelphia is attempting to halt a six-game losing streak. Skattebo is unlikely to play based on his doubtful designation, although that status does not officially rule him out. The latest verified official injury report leaves his availability unresolved, so he should not be described as inactive yet. Devin Singletary is the likely lead option if Skattebo cannot play, with Greg Desrosiers also positioned for work. The exact distribution would depend on New York’s available personnel and game plan, rather than an announced guarantee of carries. The practical takeaway entering Sunday is straightforward: Skattebo’s doubtful designation puts his participation in serious jeopardy. Philadelphia should prepare for Singletary to handle a larger role while awaiting a final decision on the Giants’ leading rusher. Skattebo is dealing with a hamstring injury that remained an issue after New York’s Week 8 bye. The second-year running back injured his hamstring during the Giants’ Week 7 victory against Houston, and the extra recovery time didn't allow him to resume a full practice workload before the Philadelphia game. away.headline: Myles Garrett injury update, latest on Rams star's status vs. Commanders
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett is set to return to the lineup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. The 30-year-old veteran set the single-season NFL sack record in 2025 with 23, and the Rams likely assumed they would get something resembling that level of production out of him. Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Garrett is expected to play on Sunday after NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Garrett was "on track to be activated" after practicing all week. Garrett was activated off of injured reserve on Saturday after he did not have a designation on the team's injury report Friday. Garrett has not played since Week 1, as he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve following the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers. L.A. made the blockbuster trade of the offseason when it acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for pass-rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, and 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Garrett was coming off the best season of his career. According to Stick to the Model's injury tracker through Week 8, the Rams have lost $37 million in player value due to injuries, the third-highest total in the NFL. Only the Packers ($42.1 million) and Patriots ($40.3 million) have lost more. The tracker calculates the value lost when a starter misses a game, with each absence costing 1/17 of what that player's grade earns at his position. Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua have accounted for two of the Rams' biggest losses, according to Stick to the Model. Garrett has missed seven games due to a knee injury, while Nacua missed two games earlier this year with a groin injury. Cornerback Trent McDuffie also missed Weeks 6 and 7 with a groin injury. Fortunately, Garrett is at least getting closer to returning from injured reserve after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Interestingly, the Rams haven't lost nearly as many games from their starters as some other teams. They've had 28 starter games missed due to injury or illness, just above the league average of 25.5 and tied for 12th-most. That makes their third-place standing in player value lost particularly notable. The Rams haven't necessarily had the most absences, but the players they've lost have carried significant value. With Watson now joining the list of season-altering injuries, Los Angeles will have to continue finding ways to overcome the attrition as it pushes through the second half of the season. away.headline: Commanders-Rams final injury report rules out two receivers, leaves McDuffie questionable
away.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their final injury report Friday ahead of their matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The report listed two of Washington's receivers, Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf), as officially OUT against the Rams. Burks missed practice all week with an injured foot that he's been dealing with since the 49ers game, while Brown was added to Thursday's report as limited before missing Friday's practice. With Terry McLaurin already out for the season, Washington will need more from Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, who led the team with seven targets and five catches for 54 yards against Philadelphia . Van Jefferson could see more work, and Luke McCaffrey is another option. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spoke Friday about Jefferson's readiness: "I liked his approach. I liked his readiness, and so when called upon, I'd expect he'd play well." Rookie Jaden Bradley could also be elevated from the practice squad, although Washington hasn't announced that move. Elsewhere on the report, Jer'Zhan Newton is questionable with his pectoral injury despite practicing fully all three days. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window and must be activated from injured reserve before he can play. That decision carries some weight with Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw now on IR . Shy Tuttle (shoulder) was limited all week but carries no game designation, while Sam Cosmi (knee) returned to full participation Friday. John Bates (shoulder) was limited throughout the week but has no game designation either. Los Angeles has some injury problems of its own, particularly in the secondary . Cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) is out, while Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable after missing every practice this week. Former Commanders safety Kam Curl (foot) is also questionable after returning to limited practice Friday. The Rams could be short-handed in the secondary, although McDuffie's and Curl's availability won't be settled until closer to kickoff. The Rams also listed long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) as doubtful, with tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), and receiver Jordan Whittington (back) questionable. Quarterback Matthew Stafford practiced fully throughout the week, while head coach Sean McVay expects Myles Garrett to play Sunday, pending his activation from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) was ruled out after injuring his hamstring in Friday’s practice . home.headline: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out
home.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM "We're still working through those types of things," McVay said Friday morning prior to practice, when asked what kind of ramp-up he expects in terms of how much Garrett is able to play on Sunday. "He's really done a great job in practice. He'll be a DNP today, but it's more of just being smart with him. Nothing to do with anything other than he has progressed really well, made a tremendous impact in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, feels really comfortable with the game plan, and it's been great having him out there, as well as (tight end) Terrance (Ferguson)." While Ferguson (ankle) also returned to practice this week, and was expected to play Sunday according to McVay, he ended up being ruled out after the Rams sent out an updated injury report. Initially listed on this week's report with an ankle injury, Ferguson picked up a hamstring injury in Friday's practice based on the injury updated report. Meanwhile, Trent McDuffie (back) and tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) are listed as questionable for Sunday's game, as well as inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and safety Kam Curl (foot). Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) is listed as doubtful, which would set up Jake McQuaide to be up from the practice squad again. McVay also said cornerback Jaylen Watson is listed as out, but will be placed on IR. Otherwise, all other Rams players listed on the injury report do not have a game status designation. For the Commanders, wide receivers Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) have been ruled out, while defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) is listed as questionable. Sure, they've barely squeaked out wins, but they've played against the likes of the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Seahawks, and Chiefs again. Denver is going to remind people that despite maybe not being a true Super Bowl-contending team, they're still a significant step above teams at the Panthers' level. away.headline: Broncos final injury report: Pat Bryant's return, depth on defense tested
away.blurb: The Broncos play the Carolina Panthers in Week 9, and it's the team's final game before the Week 10 bye, which comes at a perfect time. The team's final injury report does test the depth of this defense but also sees the return of a key rotational player on offense. All of Dondrea Tillman, Talanoa Hufanga, Kris Abrams-Draine, Brandon Jones, and Eyioma Uwazurike are either out or questionable in Week 9: Even with Bryant being listed as questionable, he'll play in Week 9: Hufanga's return will be the key to watch, and if you look at Denver's injury report from Week 8, there seems to be a good chance that the starting safety returns: In this practice week, Hufanga went DNP, Limited, and Limited and is listed as questionable. Just last week, the Broncos saw both Zach Allen and Jaylen Waddle have the exact same practice week, and both were also listed as questionable. Both played, so there is reason to believe that the Broncos took Hufanga's practice statuses this week with the same idea in mind. It does flat-out stink that the Broncos are going to still be down a starting safety with a likely Hufanga return. Jones hurt his hamstring during the win over Kansas City in Week 8 and did not practice all week. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Broncos final injury report: Pat Bryant's return, depth on defense tested . For the most part, the Denver Broncos have stayed healthy this year, but they have dealt with a good bit of injuries to primary depth, rotational players. We have already seen Jonah Coleman spent time on IR. Tyler Badie and RJ Harvey are both on IR, along with Jonah Elliss. The team has also seen Pat Bryant be placed on IR. Patrick Surtain II just recently missed time as well. All in all, Denver is certainly no strangers to injuries this year, but, for the most part, the primary starters are healthy and in a good spot. Denver Broncos final injury report for Week 9 against the Panthers In an ideal world, both Tillman and Hufanga suit up. If not, the depth of this defense is going to be tested big-time. The offense is clearly much healthier, as every one of the primary starters are healthy enough to play. I guess if we had to 'pick' one side to be hurt more, it would be the defense given how good this unit has been for years now, but that doesn't make this week's report any less shaky. The Broncos getting a win in Week 9. moving to 7-2, and having two weeks off would be the absolute best-case scenario. Denver's bye would allow every banged-up player to get healthier, and it would also present a perfect opportunity for the team to add a player or two at the NFL Trade Deadline and get them up to speed with the bye. Even in a loss, the Broncos sitting at 6-3 would still position themselves well down the stretch, especially with the ease of the remaining schedule. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: S Brandon Jones Trending Toward Inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. home.headline: Chargers final injury report before NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 and continue to shock the NFL world by showing an unwillingness to trade any of their players despite facing down a lost season in 2026. Los Angeles had hoped to right the ship and gain some momentum coming out of their week seven bye but looked listless against the Los Angeles Rams in week eight. The Chargers do have other players who may be targets on the trade market but so far the word that has been put out to insiders around the NFL is that the Chargers are continuing to execute their plan of standing pat and trying to right the ship before heading into the 2027 season. The return of Donte Jackson to field is intriguing as he has been floated as a possible trade candidate and the Chargers have built up significant young depth both on the roster and the practice squad. The Chargers have been battered by injuries this season. The joke around the NFL may be about the San Francisco 49ers electrical substation and its proximity to the practice facility but someone may need to look into the water in Los Angeles with the amount of injuries both LA teams have faced this season. By week six, the Chargers had over half of their original 53-man roster either on that week's injury report or on injured reserve. The Chargers are already down to their fifth option at left guard and despite hope for getting reinforcements to face the Houston Texans, it appears guard Kayode Awosika, who has not played since week two, is still at least one week away from returning to the field. The Chargers opened the practice windows for tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman this week but it appears that neither are ready to be activated off of injured reserve just yet. The Chargers are set to get some depth at cornerback returning to the field with Donte Jackson and rookie Rodney Shelley clear of the injury report and will carry no injury designation into the game on Sunday. The Chargers front office has been shockingly unwilling to engage with trade calls despite their record generating buzz and demand . The most obvious trade candidate, edge rusher Khalil Mack, has publicly stated that he wants to stay and head coach Jim Harbaugh has echoed that sentiment at the podium. Whether Mack is simply being a consummate professional or he really does not want to uproot and leave his family behind remains to be seen with the trade deadline just days away. If the Chargers lose to the Texans, drop to 0-8 and maintain they are not willing to trade anyone, they might no longer be operating under logic and may be relying on the force. Los Angeles is starting to get some of their injured players back and perhaps, the front office and ownership feel getting the team somewhat stable during the back half of the season and heading into the offseason is more important than a few day three draft picks. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions on Why Packers Will Beat Patriots Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have their eyes on the Super Bowl. So do the New England Patriots, who lost in last year’s Super Bowl. On Sunday, these storied teams will collide in Foxborough. The Patriots are three-point favorites. With Tom Brady on the call and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame, here are three reasons why the Packers will spoil the party and earn a statement win. 1. Depleted Patriots Offense The Patriots reached the Super Bowl last year despite the lack of a legit threat at receiver. So, they attempted to rectify that problem by signing Romeo Doubs, who had a solid four seasons with the Packers, and trading for A.J. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowler who had surpassed 1,000 yards in six of his first seven seasons. Neither player will be on the field for this game, though. Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and Brown is out again with a knee injury. Combined with the questionable status of top tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, the Packers’ strong defense will face a diluted New England attack. Without Brown and Doubs and with Henry limited to eight snaps with an injured foot, the Patriots needed to rally past the lowly Dolphins last week. The Patriots were held to merely 313 yards. The key for the Packers will be limiting the Rhamondre Stevenson-led running game and putting the pressure on New England’s passing game to make plays against a Packers defense that ranks fourth in opponent passer rating. “I think first of all, he’s an elite quarterback in the pocket, out of the pocket,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said of Drake Maye. “He’s extremely dangerous. He can make any throw. Obviously, he’s super-smart. “They got a great offensive coordinator, great receivers, great playmakers around him and, obviously, when the run game’s going they can do everything and they can throw it just as good as they can run it. So, we’re going to have our hands full for sure and got to make sure that we’re ready to play.” Prediction: The Patriots are going to have a hard time stringing together sustained success on offense. 2. Drake Maye May Screw Up Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is one of the best in the business. He was one vote away from winning NFL MVP last year. However, unless you’re one of the undisputed elite quarterbacks, a quarterback oftentimes is only as good as his supporting cast. So, while Maye is seventh in completion percentage, third in yards per attempt and fifth in touchdowns, only three quarterbacks have thrown more than Maye’s eight interceptions and his six fumbles are one off the unwelcome NFL lead. “I think speaking from playing zone coverage, they’ve got great eyes,” Maye told reporters this week. “They got eyes on the quarterback, they make plays on the football. They can, obviously, catch well. The safeties are great players. They do a lot of things well and they read the quarterback very well, mix up in zone looks. Tip balls have turned into picks that they’ve shown. “So, they’ve just had a habit of creating turnovers in the pocket with the quarterback. They have got some free rushers’ help, too, of the quarterback panicking and trying to fit some stuff to tight windows. They’re good at keeping you in some negative plays. They make you go longer distances. It’s hard.” In the Patriots’ three losses, Maye has thrown three touchdowns vs. six interceptions. In the five wins, it’s 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. His eight interceptions equal last year’s total (in less than half the attempts) are only two off his total from his rookie season in 2024. Prediction: It only takes one big mistake to swing a game between equal teams. Based on this season, Maye is more apt to make that mistake. 3. Turnovers (And Taking Advantage of Them) “The ball” is the most important thing in the sport, coach Matt LaFleur likes to say. Teams that take away and protect the ball tend to win; teams that don’t tend to lose. The Packers are tied for fourth in the league at plus-4 in turnovers. After creating only 14 takeaways last season – when Micah Parsons was on the field for 14 games – they rank second in the league with 15 takeaways this season. The Patriots this year are minus-7 overall; only the white-flag-of-surrender-waving Colts are worse at minus-11. Their 15 giveaways are the third-most in the league. Added together, you get this chart. Points Off Turnovers through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/UmVq9xw7uU The Packers are third in the league by scoring 52 points off takeaways; the Patriots are tied for 23rd with 20 points off takeaways. Green Bay’s aggressive, playmaking defense works hand-in-hand with quarterback Jordan Love’s aggressive, playmaking approach to the position. “Nobody’s had more 20-yard pass plays,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. “(Love is) a quarterback that’s wildly efficient. He has a few off-days, but they’re few and far between. They throw shots. They’ve, obviously, great speed on the edges. They have an excellent tight end, Tucker Kraft, and now getting [Josh] Jacobs back, it seems like they’re trying to work him back in there a little bit more and see what he can do for them in the red zone and things like that. I think they’ve protected better the last few games. “I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that’s an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he’s able to find [Matthew] Golden, [Christian] Watson or Tucker Kraft. Defensively, very physical. They have the second-most negative plays and created the second-most negative plays in the league. Seventeen percent of their drives end in a turnover, so that leads the league, as well.” Love is cooking. He and Kirk Cousins are the only quarterbacks with at least two touchdown passes in seven games this season. “Our goal every week is to go 1-0, and this is a very good team,” Love said. “Like you mentioned, they were in the Super Bowl last year for a reason. They’re very good in, really, all three phases. They got an elite defense. I think they do a lot of things really well. They got two really good corners on the outside. “Yeah, I got a lot of respect for them. It’s always a good test, but I think the goal for us to see how we can go out there and execute the plan, and the goal is to come away victorious. We know to put ourselves in the best position late in the season. We got to really just win every game, and that’s the mindset of going 1-0 every week. It’ll be a good test for us.” Prediction: The Packers have at least two takeaways in five consecutive games. If they can do it again, they’ll win. If the Patriots choose to activate Hollins off of IR for this game, they'd be able to get some much-needed size back at the position. Hollins hasn't played since Week 4 after dealing with a calf injury suffered in Buffalo, and returned to practice this week. Final Score Prediction: Patriots 28, Packers 23 The Patriots, despite the slow start in Miami a week ago, feel like they're on a roll. In front of a national audience with Tom Brady calling his first Patriots game, I don't see how this week ends in a loss. What it will take is Maye slinging it just like he's done the last few games and use his legs to extend some plays — as well as not letting Green Bay's rushing attack with Josh Jacobs find its footing. Forcing Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love to make poor decisions. The Packers’ pass-heavy offense averages the second-most yards through the air in the NFL, and the fewest rush yards per game. Green Bay’s 28-year-old signal caller has thrown an interception in each of his past three games, an opportunity New England may need to capitalize on. X-Factor: CB Marcus Jones This season, Green Bay has relied heavily on second-year wide receiver Matthew Golden. The speedy pass catcher sits top-10 in the NFL in both receptions and receiving yards. I expect Jones to play a major part in attempting to slow down the wideout’s production on Sunday. Not to mention, Jones’ other role for the Patriots — punt returner — is one the Packers have stuffed all season long. Green Bay allows the second-fewest yards per punt return in the NFL. From locking down a star wideout to boosting the New England offense’s field position, Jones will play a pivotal role in his team’s success on Sunday. Final Score Prediction: Packers 30, Patriots 24 I would be shocked to see the short-staffed Patriots can pull off a win over this highly touted Packers squad. New England hardly had the talent to take down Miami a week ago. With the Patriots’ receiver room still highlighted by DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, it feels hard to believe they can produce enough offensively to squeak out a win. But maybe — just maybe — a Super Bowl LI reunion, Tom Brady being back in Gillette Stadium and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame might just bring the magic New England needs come Sunday. picks.headline: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9
picks.blurb: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Lamar Jackson will reportedly miss 6-9 weeks TRENDING Yahoo Top 10 Warriors win seventh straight Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality NFL news, live updates Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 (Rich Storry-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots were able to take down the Miami Dolphins last week, improving their record to 5-3 on the season. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.

away.headline: Packers make 2 updates to week 9 injury report: Keisean Nixon DNP
away.blurb: Nixon did not practice on Thursday while dealing with a groin injury. He was listed as limited on Wednesday. The veteran has not missed a game since signing with the Packers before the 2022 season, but he might need to practice Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against the New England Patriots. Lloyd, who suffered through two injury-plagued seasons to start his NFL career, has his first injury of 2026: a knee injury. He was limited on Thursday. It's possible the Packers could return Chris Brooks this week, providing depth at running back if Lloyd can't go. Micah Parsons practiced in a limited capacity for the second straight day after returning on Wednesday. The Packers were in pads on Thursday. Parsons is not expected to play until Week 12 at the earliest. away.headline: Mack Hollins Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Patriots WR's Return Timeline Ahead of Packers Game
away.blurb: Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins is set to return to practice, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport reported on Wednesday. Hollins has missed the last four games after being placed on the injured reserved list with a calf injury. A return to practice opens a 21-day window for Hollins to be activated, but he could also make his return as soon as Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The New England Patriots may be getting much-needed reinforcements for their injury-depleted receiving corps. Hollins reeled in 15 catches for 209 yards through four games prior to his injury, but his value to the team goes beyond his statistical production. The 33-year-old wide receiver has excelled as a blocker on running plays and has been a steady veteran presence in the locker room. The Patriots has struggled to find consistent production from their wide receivers this season. Wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs headlined the Patriots' offseason acquisitions, but both players have missed significant time due to injuries. New England also parted ways with wide receivers Stefon Diggs and Kayshon Boutte, who led the team in yards and touchdowns last season, respectively. The Patriots are entering one of the toughest stretches on their schedule, and Hollins would immediately bolster a wide receiver room that dwindled down to just DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III last week. away.headline: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report
away.blurb: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Keisean Nixon, two running backs questionable for Sunday Emma Pravecek, packers.com CB Keisean Nixon GREEN BAY – The Packers have listed cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and running backs MarShawn Lloyd (knee) and Chris Brooks (ankle) as questionable for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots. Green Bay also ruled out five: linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee). Both Nixon and Lloyd popped up on the injury report during the practice week. Nixon didn't practice Thursday but returned in limited fashion Friday. He's played in 76 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. "It's always concerning when a guy doesn't practice on a Thursday but, if I know Kei like I think I do, I would expect him to put himself in a position to potentially go out there and play," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur on Friday morning. While Rhyan was ruled out, LaFleur told reporters on Thursday that he doesn't anticipate Green Bay's starting center going on IR. Rhyan hasn't practiced since injuring his ankle four snaps into the Packers' Week 7 game in Detroit. Receiver Christian Watson (ribs), guard Aaron Banks (knee) and safety Javon Bullard (personal) didn't receive game statuses and will be available Sunday. Watson broke a rib during the Packers' 27-19 win over Carolina but returned to finish the game. He wore protective padding while practicing in a limited capacity this week. home.headline: Mack Hollins Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Patriots WR's Return Timeline Ahead of Packers Game
home.blurb: Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins is set to return to practice, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport reported on Wednesday. Hollins has missed the last four games after being placed on the injured reserved list with a calf injury. A return to practice opens a 21-day window for Hollins to be activated, but he could also make his return as soon as Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The New England Patriots may be getting much-needed reinforcements for their injury-depleted receiving corps. Hollins reeled in 15 catches for 209 yards through four games prior to his injury, but his value to the team goes beyond his statistical production. The 33-year-old wide receiver has excelled as a blocker on running plays and has been a steady veteran presence in the locker room. The Patriots has struggled to find consistent production from their wide receivers this season. Wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs headlined the Patriots' offseason acquisitions, but both players have missed significant time due to injuries. New England also parted ways with wide receivers Stefon Diggs and Kayshon Boutte, who led the team in yards and touchdowns last season, respectively. The Patriots are entering one of the toughest stretches on their schedule, and Hollins would immediately bolster a wide receiver room that dwindled down to just DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III last week. Predicting the Raiders' Week 9 Moves In their Week 8 matchup against the Jets, Las Vegas made several notable changes to their starting lineup that proved fruitful. After struggling to find competent play at the right guard position between Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers, the Raiders turned to rookie Trey Zuhn. The Raiders need Porter beyond just this week. Resting Porter on Sunday is far from ideal for Sunday's game, but may be best for his career, depending on the severity of his injury and how much progress he made on it during the week. Porter sitting out would offer a valuable opportunity to other corners on the roster. Porter may very well start against the 49ers. Regardless, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses is sure to see significant playing time. Heading into Sunday, Masses could be in for another action-packed day, who has had extreme highs and lows during this season. “I think it’s always a moving target. See where your team’s at, and who’s playing the best ball at the time. And it’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. And [there have] been changes at guard," Kubiak said earlier this week. "[We have] changed up front defensively. Changed at corner, and that’s the NFL. We have a young roster, and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best." picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers expert picks and predictions ahead of Week 9 kickoff - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Lamar Jackson will reportedly miss 6-9 weeks TRENDING Yahoo Top 10 Warriors win seventh straight Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality NFL news, live updates Raiders vs. 49ers expert picks and predictions ahead of Week 9 kickoff Marvin Uzor, Raiders Wire · Raiders Wire Sat, November 7, 2026 at 11:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Last week, the experts split almost evenly on Raiders vs. Jets , and the believers walked away looking smart. Seven days later, the panel has made up its mind. Across the 21 straight-up picks rounded up here, every single one goes to the San Francisco 49ers. There is a twist hiding in the scores, though. Seven of the 11 national score predictions have the Raiders losing by single digits, which would be enough to cover the spread. The Raiders Wire staff went 4-0 for the 49ers, with an average score of 31-23. LaMarr Fields had the widest margin at 34-23, pointing to a 49ers ground game the Raiders haven't been able to stop. NFL.com sees no drama All five NFL.com analysts took the 49ers, and nobody on that panel is harsher than Jeremy Bergman at 40-24. Bobby Kownack went 28-17, while Gennaro Filice (35-27), Dan Parr (34-26) and Brooke Cersosimo (28-20) kept it within eight. Only Bergman and Kownack have the 49ers winning by double digits. Cersosimo pointed to a familiar face on San Francisco's defensive line. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, reacquired from the Indianapolis Colts during the bye, is set for his second debut with the 49ers. "Buckner's addition should pay dividends for San Francisco moving forward, beginning Sunday against the visiting Raiders," Cersosimo wrote. She also acknowledged San Francisco's turnover problems before the bye, but she still gave the 49ers the edge in most major categories. CBS Sports and ESPN agree on the winner At CBS Sports, Pete Prisco has the 49ers winning 31-17 , while John Breech sees a tighter game at 30-23. ESPN's writers all picked San Francisco as well, with Pamela Maldonado at 24-20, Seth Walder at 29-23 and Eric Moody at 34-20. ESPN's Football Power Index gives the 49ers an 83.6% chance to win, a number that backs up the panel. Pro Football Talk expects a fight Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk also landed on 24-20, tied with Maldonado for the closest call among the national picks. He sounds ready for a scrap. "In a renewal of a rivalry so intense that they had to stop playing each other in the preseason, the Raiders will make it interesting," Florio wrote. The spread is where Raiders fans find friends USA TODAY's six experts, including Jarrett Bell and Nate Davis, went 6-0 for the 49ers straight up. Against the spread, Bleacher Report's panel leans Las Vegas 4-3 , with Gary Davenport, Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski taking the points. Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox and Moe Moton laid them. Hanford admitted that "everything logical here is telling me to take the 49ers to win this one going away." He still expects quarterback Kirk Cousins to hit enough big plays to keep it within single digits, calling it a game that "just feels like a backdoor cover." Picking the Raiders to win on Sunday is a lonely spot this week. Picking them to keep it respectable is a crowded one. away.headline: Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism
away.blurb: On Wednesday, the official injury report listed defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi and tight end Ian Thomas as limited participants. Cornerback Darien Porter missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury he suffered against the Jets. On Thursday, Las Vegas' injury report remained minimal. Porter returned to practice on Thursday, which is good news for the Raiders' young defensive backfield. He was a limited participant, and Thomas was a full participant. Booker did not practice on Thursday. Dont'e Thornton was limited as well. Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism Skip to main content SI.COM The Las Vegas Raiders are just a few days away from facing the San Francisco 49ers on the road. Las Vegas went back to work on Thursday, looking to build upon their Week 9 win over the New York Jets. Las Vegas' success this season has largely depended on the quality of the opponent they face. The Raiders have played well enough to beat four of the league's worst teams, but have struggled against the league's elite, which the 49ers are. Still, those four wins are more than the Raiders had all last season, and they are unquestionably better than last season. It may have been against the Jets, but Las Vegas aims to translate its second-half success against New York to this Sunday against the 49ers. After struggling in the third quarter all season, the Raiders' offense exploded against the Jets. In Week 8, Kirk Cousins led the Raiders downfield to score on their first offensive drive after halftime for the first time all season. It was more than impactful, as it led to Las Vegas producing their best third quarter of the season. The Raiders must continue to play well on offense to help their defense. “I think the first play of the second half might have been the throw to Brock [Bowers], and I thought that was a key play in the game and a great call by our coaches, and that whole drive, to finish that drive, it got us right back in the game, which we needed, very important," Cousins said earlier this week. “If you punt and they go down and score, it could be a whole different story. So, it’s very important, and we’ve got to be really strong in the third quarter the rest of the way. And I felt we have continued, last week in the fourth quarter, continuing to play well in the fourth quarter. But it’s a four-quarter game. You’ve got to do it, all four of them.” Throughout the rest of the season, Las Vegas needs the Cousins who showed up in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets to show up in each of their next three games. Moving forward, they will need that version of Cousins and their offense even before the third quarter. Fatukasi was a full participant as well. Based on their injury report, Las Vegas appears to be the healthiest it has been this season, as their Week 1 injury report listed stars Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers. The Raiders will likely give rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses a bigger role

Brandon Aiyuk and his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, appeared outside of the San Francisco 49ers ' business offices on Friday, making a statement about his NFL return. A trade would need to occur quickly, as the NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. By Matthew Couden Contributing Writer Aiyuk tore his ACL, MCL, and meniscus in his right knee in a game against the Kansas City Chiefs in October 2024 and hasn't played since. After drama between him and the 49ers over his missed mandatory rehab sessions, among other issues, the former 2020 first-round pick is now working towards NFL reinstatement. After reportedly filing paperwork to be reinstated from the reserve/left-squad list that the 49ers put him on, a meeting with the team could help him move towards that goal. "You know, feeling great, feeling healthy. It's a long recovery process. A long rehab process. But I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated in the National Football League," Aiyuk said in a brief statement to reporters on Friday. San Francisco 49ers GM John Lynch suggested that "everything is possible" regarding a reunion between Aiyuk and the team. According to ESPN , head coach Kyle Shanahan made a very similar remark. More news: 2 Clear Favorites Emerge to Trade for Ravens RB Derrick Henry Ahead of meeting with the team on Friday, Aiyuk's agent shut down questions on which team his client might play for after NFL reinstatement. "Don't really have any comment about where he's going to play. We'll keep that between us and the Niners, but, obviously, we're here with all the right intentions," Rosenhaus told reporters. According to The Associated Press , the NFL told Aiyuk he owes about $13 million to the 49ers in bonus forfeitures. These are connected to the four-year, $120 million extension that Aiyuk signed in 2024. home.headline: 49ers’ Brandon Aiyuk must jump multiple hurdles before NFL return becomes official
home.blurb: 49ers news: Brandon Aiyuk must jump multiple hurdles before NFL return is official NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics San Francisco 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk faces reinstatement and financial hurdles as his NFL return remains unresolved after talks this week. Add ClutchPoints on Google San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk still faces financial and roster questions after meeting with the team Friday as he pursues a return to the NFL. MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes Aiyuk and newly hired agent Drew Rosenhaus visited the organization’s business offices near Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California. The 28-year-old has remained on the reserve/left squad list since December 2025. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport outlined the obstacles Saturday on X, formerly Twitter, sharing a clip from “The Insiders.” “He did not. Has not officially been reinstated to try to get on the 49ers roster. That has not happened. Now there are several issues here.” From The Insiders on @nflnetwork : Brandon Aiyuk came and went on Friday, exiting the #49ers facility with no resolution. pic.twitter.com/2P7kvXq78w — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 7, 2026 The NFL sent Aiyuk and the NFLPA a letter Thursday regarding bonuses the league says he must repay to the 49ers. Rapoport described a disagreement over the amount. “The NFL believes that is 13 million. The NFLPA believes the number is a little less. We'll see where they land if there's a negotiation.” Aiyuk signed a four-year , $120 million extension before the 2024 season after earning second-team All-Pro honors in 2023. Arbitration could prolong the repayment dispute. He has not played since suffering a multi-ligament knee injury on October 20, 2024. Even reinstatement would not necessarily force an immediate roster move, Rapoport explained. “My understanding is the NFL is expected to give a two-week roster exemption if he gets reinstated, which means the 49ers wouldn't have to do anything immediately anyway.” The trade deadline arrives Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET/1 p.m. PT, but general manager John Lynch has said he does not expect Aiyuk to play for San Francisco again. The Seahawks are 9.5-point favorites and 77% on the moneyline, with the Cardinals at 23%, but Gardner Minshew can spark this Arizona offense to stay within the number and push this game Over the 38.5-point total. Kickoff is Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. Don't miss the rest of our NFL picks to stay ahead of the action this weekend. TOP PICK Cardinals vs Seahawks prediction: Over 38.5 The Over 38.5 sits at 52% , and while nobody expected a Gardner Minshew vs. Drew Lock battle two weeks ago, it sets us up for a high-scoring game. Lock threw three touchdown passes in Week 2 when these teams met, finishing with a 139.1 QB rating, as the Seattle Seahawks scored 31 points. With Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet returning last week, their ground game improved, as did their pass protection, which will help Lock. A week of practice puts Minshew in a strong position after a sensational cameo last week. He added some much-needed juice to this offense, throwing three touchdowns. His 75% completion percentage on passes of 20+ yards was a huge increase from Jacoby Brissett , who had averaged 20.7% across the season. Cardinals vs Seahawks combo We don't know exactly how healthy Lock is, given he's been inactive for two weeks, which limits my optimism about backing the Seahawks. The return of their starting running backs is big, but the blocking hasn't helped, and the team ranks 29th overall in EPA/rush. Conversely, the Arizona Cardinals ' ground game is in rude health, ranking 10th in EPA/rush. The Cardinals' defense is also improving, allowing 5.02 yards per play across the past two games , a drop of more than one yard from the 6.18 it allowed in Weeks 1-5. Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains the Seahawks' main threat and is QB-proof. He's scored nine times this season, four of them with Lock at QB, and has the sixth-most red-zone targets of any WR. Cardinals +9.5 Jaxon Smith-Njigba anytime touchdown Cardinals vs Seahawks touchdown scorer: Trey McBride The Seahawks have allowed only two touchdowns to tight ends, but Trey McBride isn't a normal TE, and this is a good spot for him. He has five touchdowns this season, including one against the Seahawks in Week 2, and has found the end zone in each of his past two games. He also leads the entire NFL in red-zone targets with 19 and has 10 targets inside the 10-yard line . The QB change shouldn't impact him much either, given that Minshew targeted him eight times on 23 passing attempts. I'd play this up to 35%. away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Weather Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Ex-NFL star Antonio Brown avoids jail time as part of plea deal after Miami shooting Winners, losers as Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 on Thursday Night Football An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). away.headline: Seahawks QB Drew Lock to play through severe elbow injury vs Cardinals
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks are set to take on the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 with backup quarterback Drew Lock after starter Sam Darnold was ruled out with a quad injury. However, it turns out Lock is dealing with a bit of a serious injury of his own. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Lock has been battling severe tendinitis in his throwing elbow, but the Seahawks are still comfortable with having him start on Sunday against the Cardinals after he looked good in limited practice reps this week. Brandon Aiyuk Makes Strong Statement on NFL Return Before 49ers Meeting It’s good news that the Seahawks still feel comfortable in Lock’s ability to play and play well this week, but this injury update is certainly a cause for concern, especially because it is affecting his throwing arm. So, it will be worth monitoring up until kickoff on Sunday and even throughout the game because if he is unable to play, the Seahawks would be forced to turn to former 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe. Lock has already filled in quite nicely for Darnold two times this season, completing 35 of his 48 pass attempts for 422 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions, but that was when he was healthy. That could be why the Seahawks are so comfortable with rolling with him this week, though. Every win also matters in the NFC West as Seattle currently sits in second place with a 4-4 record. The San Francisco 49ers are in the top spot at 6-1. A second-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft, Lock has thrown for 6,769 yards, 38 touchdowns and 28 interceptions in his professional career. home.headline: Sam Darnold injured, latest rumors as QB in danger of missing more games for Seahawks
home.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals and reportedly may also be out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders. ESPN's Adam Schefter , citing league sources, reported on Sunday that Darnold "is in danger of missing Seattle's Week 10 game against the Raiders." Schefter added that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it is the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. Drew Lock is dealing with an elbow injury but if available is slated to start with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals, Macdonald said. The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week. Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (4-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (6-1). A win this week over the Cardinals (3-5) would increase the defending champions' playoff odds to 54 percent, while a loss would drop the team to 29 percent, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . The Bears are now 6-2 and in the driver’s seat to make the playoffs in the NFC with the halfway point of the season nearing. Meanwhile, Tampa Bay is 2-0 since quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb) returned to action and 3-1 over the last four weeks after an 0-4 start. The Bucs are set as underdogs in this matchup, but their defense (No. 1 in EPA/Play this season) may be one of the best options to slow down this high-octane Bears attack. Tampa Bay is only a half game out of the NFC South lead, and a win over the Bears would do wonders for this team’s playoff chances. Can Mayfield and Co. make it happen on the road? The Bucs are 3-5, and a win over this Bears team would give them a big boost before their bye. It certainly won't be easy, though, and our staff doesn't think so, either. As always, our picks are in for this upcoming matchup — here's how we see this crucial Week 9 game turning out: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Bears 21, Bucs 20 The Bucs have ripped off two straight W’s and know their identity is built on the run game and great defense. They will need both vs. the Bears on SNF. Chicago owns one of the best offenses in the league, led by Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, and their defense got even more stout up front with the addition of Jeffrey Simmons. However, the Bucs can exploit their secondary, which means Baker Mayfield will have to throw the ball. It will be the real first test of his thumb. I think the Bucs are able to keep things close despite this being a tough challenge. However, they fall just short. Overall Record: 4-4 James Hill, Writer: Bears 24, Bucs 14 This is a game where I think the Bucs fall back down to earth a little bit. The team is facing one of the best offenses in the NFL that just had a great defensive showing against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks. If Baker Mayfield and the passing game can’t get going, this could be a long game. Overall Record: 3-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bears 24, Bucs 17 For the first time in over a year, the Bucs have won back-to-back games. It's a step in the right direction, sure, but they've still got a lot of work to do to dig themselves out of the hole they created for themselves by going 0-4 to start the season. We still don't really know if Baker Mayfield can throw the ball down the field after returning from his thumb injury, and the Bears present all sorts of problems on both sides of the ball. The Bucs' defense may be legit, but that won't be enough to knock off the Bears in Chicago. Overall Record: 5-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Bears 28, Bucs 24 I’m getting my popcorn out for the battle between Todd Bowles’ defense and Ben Johnson’s offense. This is going to be fun. I think it’s going to be a close-scoring game, but Baker Mayfield is going to have to shake off the rust, which he told us earlier this week shouldn’t be an issue. Still, it’s gonna have to get going a bit to allow for the run game to open up. Stopping Caleb Williams won’t be easy, but right now, Bowles has been the old Bowles we all know — terrorizing offenses. I think Tampa Bay keeps it close but in the end, on prime time, they don’t pull it off. River Wells, Editor: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Every week, I doubt Tampa Bay, and the last two weeks, they've proven me wrong. Were it another opponent, I would be more open to picking Tampa Bay this time around — but this Chicago Bears team is very, very good. Caleb Williams is unstoppable when he isn't getting in his own way, and he's been crisp and consistent for two weeks. Ben Johnson is the best playcaller in football, and the Bears will be defending home turf after a big win against Seattle the Monday prior. The Bucs have a strong running game and an elite defense. But the passing game remains nonexistent (literally, in some cases), and the offense won't be enough to outscore the Bears in this contest. Consensus: Bears 5, Bucs 0 Things were more even last week, but this week, our staff is all Bears. We're betting that Chicago's well-rounded team and the addition of Jeffery Simmons will be enough to knock off a Bucs team still looking to find its identity. That being said, the Bucs have a chance with this defense. And if they win? Tampa Bay's momentum couldn't be higher entering the bye week. Baker Mayfield and the Bucs won in Week 8 without completing a pass, and after an 0-4 start they’ve won three of their last four games to put themselves right back in the mix to win a terrible NFC South. The Bucs have back-to-back division wins over Carolina and Atlanta, but things will be a lot tougher on the road against the Bears and an MVP candidate in Williams . Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. The Bears have also scored at least 30 points in every game that Williams has completed this season, making them one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Oddsmakers have set Chicago as a six-point favorite at home as it looks to get to 7-2 before a Week 10 bye. The Bears are still behind the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings – who beat them earlier this season – in the NFC North standings. Tampa Bay’s defense is now No. 1 in EPA/Play after picking off Michael Penix Jr. several times in a rain-soaked matchup in Week 8, but things won’t be nearly as easy against Williams. On the bright side for the Bucs, they should be able to run the ball (eighth in EPA/Rush this season) against a Bears defense that is allowing 4.4 yards per carry in 2026. Chicago traded for star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons ahead of Week 8, but the Tampa Bay running game – led by Bucky Irving – won’t be easy to stop on Sunday night. I lean with the Bears to win this game, and it’ll be interesting to see if the odds move at all with both teams trending in the right direction with the halfway point of the 2026 season upon us. "Schematically, it's very challenging to run the ball, and then when you have the talent on the defensive line and in the linebacker crew that they have, you know, those are tough yards to come by." picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Lamar Jackson will reportedly miss 6-9 weeks TRENDING Yahoo Top 10 Warriors win seventh straight Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality NFL news, live updates Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders.
