picks.headline: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills
picks.blurb: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Lamar Jackson will reportedly miss 6-9 weeks TRENDING Yahoo Top 10 Warriors win seventh straight Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality NFL news, live updates Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills (Gregory Fisher-USA TODAY Sports) Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) have a pivotal matchup on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." Jefferson's frustrations have drawn questions about the player throwing him the football. It's not surprising that there have been questions given all the pieces that the Vikings have on offense. It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. We'll keep a close eye on what moves head coach Kevin O'Connell makes when the matchup gets underway with Buffalo.

picks.headline: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills
picks.blurb: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Lamar Jackson will reportedly miss 6-9 weeks TRENDING Yahoo Top 10 Warriors win seventh straight Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality NFL news, live updates Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kevin O'Connell has spent the week calling Kyler Murray his starter, but a hamstring may make that call for him. NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero said Thursday on KFAN's Power Trip Morning Show that he expects Carson Wentz to start for the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, days after Murray struggled through the loss in Detroit . "I would lean toward it being Carson Wentz," Pelissero said on KFAN . He described the hamstring as legitimate but not major, and said Minnesota may not want to risk a quarterback who relies on his legs at less than full speed. Carson Wentz has already won two games Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell talks to quarterback Kyler Murray (1) during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Wentz isn't a stranger to this offense. He played most of the 39-22 opener against Green Bay after replacing Murray early and threw three touchdown passes, then started the 9-3 win in Chicago. He has 276 passing yards and no interceptions this season, and Minnesota won both games. Those wins weren't pretty, though. The offense scored nine points at Soldier Field, and Wentz was sacked six times across the two games. Behind a line that has allowed 21 sacks, the Vikings would be trading mobility for a quarterback who has to get the ball out on time. Murray has 1,022 passing yards, five touchdown passes and three interceptions, and he's been sacked 15 times. He has also run for 167 yards on 29 carries, which is why a sore hamstring matters more for him than it would for most quarterbacks. O'Connell said Monday he isn't considering a performance benching and Murray is still the starter when healthy, per ESPN. "I don't think we're there yet," he said of a possible absence , adding that he would keep getting updates from the medical staff. Pelissero's take lands after Nick Kostos argued the Vikings can't keep waiting on Murray . Pelissero also said he sees a low chance of a major trade before the Nov. 10 deadline, which leaves the job between the two quarterbacks already in the building. Either one draws a tough assignment. Buffalo's Greg Rousseau has seven sacks, and Josh Allen brings the NFL's most efficient offense to U.S. Bank Stadium, so Brian Flores' defense may need to carry the night again. O'Connell's Thursday press availability should offer the next clue. away.headline: Vikings-Bills First Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he’ll play or not. Kevin O’Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson’s absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the ‘playing through it’ variety and don’t seem like they’ll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he’ll play or not. Kevin O’Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson’s absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the ‘playing through it’ variety and don’t seem like they’ll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins did not practice Thursday with a rib injury, nor did starting guard Alec Andreesen, with an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. We’ll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Saturday.
